case.case_title: Wijenayake and Others v. Amerasena and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC (FR) 290/98, decided on 1 September 1999

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the Petitioners were lawfully detained and brought before a judge in accordance with Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The Petitioners claimed they were detained overnight unlawfully and were not properly brought before a judge with legal authority for their detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: The Respondents contended that the Petitioners were produced before the Magistrate at the earliest opportunity and that their detention was lawful under the circumstances.
key_facts: Petitioners were detained overnight at the Matara Police Station after arrest on 4 November 1997.
Petitioners were produced before the Magistrate the next day; two were remanded and one released on bail.
The Magistrate acquitted the Petitioners on all charges.
Petitioners alleged mistreatment and unlawful detention during this period.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 13(2) as requiring that any detained person must be promptly brought before a judicial authority and that detention without legal order is prohibited.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found that although the Petitioners were produced before the Magistrate, the detention and arrest lacked lawful justification. The Magistrate's acquittal and the circumstances of the detention indicated a violation of Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention must be lawful and persons detained must be promptly brought before a judge.
Unjustified detention violates fundamental rights under Article 13(2).

outcome.holding: The Court held that the Petitioners' detention was unlawful and violated Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The Respondents were ordered to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the Court's finding that the Petitioners were unlawfully detained without proper legal order, reinforcing the violation of their fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Petitioners were detained overnight and produced before the Magistrate the next day, but the Court found no justification for the detention given the acquittal and circumstances.
